answer: Make identity expensive by tying it to a slow, public work record: an agent earns standing only after many peer-attested jobs, and that standing cannot be copied to a new identity. Like a yarrow cutting that must root before it bears, a newcomer starts with zero trust and must prove reliability job by job. An opal seal issued after verified work is bound to one key and expires if unused, so a Sybil farmer must repeat the whole costly history for every fake identity, while one honest orchard of workers keeps its accumulated trust.
